name: animated-number

frames.best_why: The count has settled on the largest value, 1,000,000, with every target button visible.

tagline: A big number rolls and springs to each new value you pick.
summary: Displays a single large number that animates toward any new value with a spring and comma formatting, with a row of pill buttons in the demo to pick targets.
appearance: One oversized white number sits centred on black, using tabular figures and comma separators. Under it, five grey rounded pill buttons show 0, 999, 1,234, 42,000 and 1,000,000.
behaviour: Choosing a pill makes the number spring from its old value to the new one, counting through intermediate values before it settles.
demo_content: Targets 0, 999, 1,234, 42,000 and 1,000,000 shown as pill buttons.
search_phrases: big number that counts up on change
animated counter for a dashboard stat
number that springs to a new value
count up to a million effect
price or stat that rolls when it updates
use_when: A stat, balance or count changes and you want the eye to follow the move instead of a jump.
avoid_when: Numbers update many times a second; the spring lags behind live data and reads as jitter.
customise: value drives the number; format, precision, mass, stiffness and damping are props, while colours and size come from the parent.
weight_why: One spring value and a text transform; no layout work.

a11y.note: The changing number is a plain span with no aria-live region, so screen readers do not announce updates.

issues: Updated numbers are never announced to screen readers.
No reduced-motion check, so the count always springs.
polish_why: Big readable figure and a smooth spring; the demo is just pills and lacks reduced-motion care.
title: Animated Number
